findings.text: Module removal is privileged and serialized. The caller needs capability CAP_SYS_MODULE and the global disable flag must be clear, otherwise permission failure is reported. A bounded user supplied name with length governed by MODULE_NAME_LEN is validated, audited, then resolved under the global module lock with interruptible acquisition. Removal is refused with EWOULDBLOCK or EBUSY style errors while dependents remain, while lifecycle state is not live, and when an init routine lacks a matching exit routine unless forced unloading is allowed. On acceptance the target is marked as dying while still locked, then after unlocking its exit callback and notification hooks run, pending asynchronous work is drained, diagnostic data about the last unload including flags is retained, backing storage is released and waiters on the module queue are awakened.

Loadable modules move among coming and live and going and unformed. Only live accepts a removal request, and acceptance moves the module to going while still preventing new users. Final teardown later moves it to unformed while retaining list membership briefly to block duplicate loads, then unlinks it from list and address tree. Visible state reporting distinguishes live and coming and going, with going shown with a minus marker and coming with a plus marker when state display is requested alongside taint enclosure.

Reference accounting uses a large bias established at load time and known as MODULE_REF_BASE. Release subtracts that bias and a negative outcome is forbidden. A nonzero remainder shows concurrent users and triggers an attempt to restore the bias unless the count has reached zero. Acquisition increments the count when the target exists and emits a trace event. The user visible count attribute reflects the unbiased value.

A single global module mutex serializes name lookup and dependency checks and state checks and owner name capture during dependency resolution and usage link removal and list plus tree mutation including transition to unformed and final unlink. It is not held across the exit callback and notification dispatch and full asynchronous drain during removal. Symbol release paths and tainted list scans use read side critical sections, with the tainted scan additionally requiring the mutex to be held, and final list removal uses delayed unlink followed by a grace period before descriptor storage and lock class ranges are released.

Paired acquire and release operations manage symbol references. Acquisition looks up a name under a read side section, accepts only GPL restricted symbols with a diagnostic otherwise, attempts to hold the owner, and returns the resolved value or null on failure. Release by name revalidates existence under a read side section and drops the owner hold. Release by address ignores core kernel text and otherwise resolves the owning executable region under a read side section before dropping the hold.

Per kind module storage is described by a base pointer plus a length plus a read execute only flag. Allocation rounds length to page granularity, selects data versus text backing based on kind, obtains writable backing, records whether the backing is execute only, excludes non execute only blocks from leak reporting, zeroes the block and records the base. Teardown releases lock classes for every populated kind, defers data kind until last because it hosts the module descriptor itself, and delegates backing release to the executable memory allocator. Text kinds with the execute only flag have protections restored through a dedicated helper.

Sysfs presence is dismantled as a grouping of dependency links for unloadable builds plus informational attributes with per attribute release callbacks plus parameter entries plus driver and holder directory references plus note and section groups plus a synchronous object release that waits on a local completion. Section and note groups when present are removed as groups, their binary attribute name storage and group storage are freed immediately under an assumption of no concurrent users, and cleared. Disabled builds provide empty variants for section and note removal.

Taint is a bitmask rendered as a compact run of per flag characters enclosed in parentheses when any bit is set or when state display forces enclosure, with distinct markers for going versus coming. A requester using GPL restricted symbols while depending on a proprietary owner is rejected, otherwise proprietary use propagates the proprietary bit with a diagnostic. Forced loading records a forced taint when permitted and is otherwise rejected with an exec format error. Unloaded tainted modules are remembered in a list keyed by name with overlapping taint bits incrementing a counter, otherwise a new entry with count one is added, with allocation failure reported as out of memory.

Dependency resolution grants GPL access only to non proprietary requesters, records use of GPL restricted symbols, validates proprietary inheritance plus version agreement plus namespace import, and holds the provider on success. Lookup and provider name capture occur under the global mutex with a sleep annotation due to possible contention. Callers needing an initializing provider block on a module wait queue until resolution no longer reports busy, up to a bounded delay of 30 times the clock tick rate, then emit a diagnostic if the wait expired.

Symbol namespaces with a module prefix carry a comma separated list of allowed consumer names where a trailing star denotes prefix matching. A requester matches when its name equals an entry or has the entry as prefix for star entries. A namespaced symbol is accepted when the provider namespace grants the requester through that mechanism or when the requester declares the namespace in its import list, otherwise a diagnostic is emitted and rejection depends on whether missing imports are configured as tolerated.

Module information is stored as a packed sequence of null terminated tag pairs with zero padding bounded by a section size that is decremented while scanning. Advancement skips non zero bytes then padding and fails when the bound is exhausted. Lookup scans from the section start or from a prior match for a tag followed by an equals sign and returns the value portion, supporting iteration over repeated tags such as namespace imports.

Version agreement is vacuous when the exporter supplies no checksum. When extended checksum data exists the loader searches it for the symbol name and accepts only on exact checksum equality, warning once when the symbol is absent and then accepting. Without extended data an absent version table triggers a forced load attempt. Otherwise a legacy table is scanned for a name match with exact checksum equality required, mismatch produces a diagnostic and rejection, while a completely missing entry warns once and is tolerated as a toolchain gap.

Several misuse cases are treated as unrecoverable. Release of the load bias must never drive the count negative, flag formatting must never observe the unformed state, symbol release must resolve its target, address based release must resolve a non core address to an owner, and state display must observe only live plus coming plus going. These checks signal caller or accounting errors rather than expected failures.

Each module exposes a stable set of informational attributes with fixed access modes and value shapes. Attributes named taint plus refcnt plus initstate plus coresize plus datasize plus initsize appear as readable values with mode 0444 terminated by newline, while the event file with mode 0200 is writable and synthesizes an event from the written payload. Lifecycle values use distinct lowercase words for live plus coming plus going. Size values aggregate per kind lengths by class, with core size including text plus core data unless data is required to live in separate virtual allocation, and taint renders as the compact flag run.

Final release keeps the module discoverable only until its state is moved to unformed, then performs architecture plus unload specific cleanup plus parameter destruction, with live patch modules additionally releasing executable format state. List and address tree unlink occur under lock with delayed list semantics, followed by a grace period before the descriptor can be freed and before lock class ranges are released. Per CPU state and init section release precede the final per kind memory sweep.

Architecture specific cleanup and init section release default to no operation through weak definitions that a port may override. Builds without unload support replace dependency release and unload initialization with trivial operations that respectively do nothing and report success, and dependency acquisition in that configuration is a direct provider hold attempt. Section and note teardown likewise collapse to empty operations when the corresponding feature is disabled.
